parsed.elsewhere_quote: If a prime $p$ occurs in any $C\in\mathcal C$, Lemma 2 supplies a terminal $D\in\mathcal C$ containing $p$. Therefore every prime occurring in any member of $\mathcal C$ belongs to $P$. It follows that every member of $\mathcal C$ is a subset of the finite set $P$, and hence $\mathcal C$ itself is finite
parsed.explanation: The quoted induction leaves two routine details implicit: after applying induction to the deleted sets, restore the deleted element to the common core; deleting a common element preserves distinctness. These follow immediately and do not create a gap. The resulting bounded-size finiteness lemma, together with Lemma 2 and the terminal-member argument, proves the required finite-prime dependence for all accepted supports.
